rationale:
I judge the `{cite}` on `src/authoring/usage.rs#struct[UsageLog]` to be the right role for `requirements.authoring.usage_storage`.

- **Not a test.** `UsageLog` is a production type, so `{test}` does not apply.
- **Not an `{impl}` root.** The struct decides and checks nothing, and it has no serialization attributes.
  - The format fields the requirement lists are in `UsageRecord`: version, run, project root, subject, start and end time, outcome, determination, `evidence_output` and `evidence_written`. Only that type is `#[derive(Serialize)]`.
  - The path logic and the writes are in `UsageLog::start`, `finish` and `save`. Those methods already carry their own `{impl}` markers for the related requirements `requirements.configuration.state_location` and `requirements.authoring.usage_requests`.
  - Persisting the record and flagging evidence written or not is carried out in `src/authoring/mod.rs`, where `persisted`, `failed`, `author_evidence_with_output` and `prepare_assessment` are marked `{impl}`.
  - `UsageLog` only holds the per-run `record` and its `path` (the separate JSON file), plus transient bookkeeping: `started`, `seen`, `active_request` and `first_request_finished`. It is reached from those marked items, so it needs no `{impl}` of its own.
- **`{cite}` is right.** The struct is the in-memory counterpart of the per-assessment, persisted usage record. It pairs the `record` with the `path` it is saved to. A change to the stored-record requirement, such as where the file lives, what the record holds, or the one-record-per-run rule, could require changing this type. That makes it a relied-upon form, which is what `{cite}` is for.
- **No redundancy.** The struct has no `{impl}` or `{test}` reference to the same requirement. The `{test}` markers on the `mod[tests]` functions belong to other items.

I found no gap.

text: Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
